title: Choose CodeQuest's new visual world
question: Choose the visual system that should govern student, teacher, and admin screens.

options.label: Incident Command Grid
options.lineage: emergency operations boards and civil-defense field stations
options.thesis: CodeQuest becomes a shared operations room where every role sees live state, priority, and the next executable action.
options.viewport: A wide command board pairs a compact role rail with one dominant work zone, live status bands, and a precise queue of next actions.
options.risk: The system can feel militarized if operational language overwhelms learning language.

raised.raise: Major tasks expose clear reversible previews and explicit commit points.
Navigation and state labels say exactly what they control.
Role color appears only at edges, status bands, and active controls.
Each role gets one unmistakable color field without fragmenting the system.

options.label: Repair Field Manual
options.lineage: technical service manuals, exploded diagrams, and annotated repair logs
options.thesis: Every screen reads like a repair manual opened to the exact procedure, evidence, and diagnostic state the role needs now.
options.viewport: Tabbed chapters frame a large procedural workspace with diagrams, numbered steps, and margin diagnostics.
options.risk: Its documentation familiarity can make high-energy learning moments feel too instructional.

options.label: HyperCard Workshop
options.thesis: Roles move through linked cards whose controls look editable, direct, and handmade.
options.viewport: A fixed card workspace holds the current task while a visible trail preserves context and backtracking.
options.case: It strongly identifies with learning and making, but loses dense teacher and admin clarity to the command grid.
options.risk: Large analytics tables fight the fixed-card metaphor.

options.label: Memory Void Console
options.thesis: Courses, students, and system areas become luminous objects arranged in a calm black spatial field.
options.viewport: A selected role object rises from a dark field while its immediate actions orbit as smaller controls.
options.case: It gives CodeQuest a memorable digital identity, but spatial navigation weakens repeated operational scanning.
options.risk: Motion and depth can slow routine teacher and admin work.

options.label: Amber Darkroom
options.lineage: printing darkrooms and timed chemical stations
options.thesis: Learning state develops through staged stations with previews before commitment.
options.viewport: A linear station view moves work through compose, test, commit, inspect, and complete.
options.case: The sequence is clear, but the photography ritual does not identify with CodeQuest's users.
options.risk: Amber monotony weakens role and status distinction.

options.label: Quoted Industrial
options.lineage: industrial streetwear labels and stockroom wayfinding
options.thesis: Literal labels, hazard geometry, and tagged active states make the interface impossible to misread.
options.viewport: Large quoted zone labels divide a strict monochrome grid with one orange active tag.
options.case: Wayfinding is excellent, but the fashion reference competes with the learning system.
options.kept: Literal labels and decisive active states.
options.risk: The visual attitude can overpower educational content.

options.label: Iridescent Evidence
options.lineage: iridescent cloud edges and scientific observation plates
options.thesis: Quiet evidence fields reserve spectral color for uncertain, forming, and active states.
options.viewport: Wide evidence panels use nearly colorless fields with narrow role and state bands.
options.case: It is legible and calm, but lacks the urgency and identity CodeQuest needs.
options.kept: Color appears only where it carries state.
options.risk: The system could feel like a generic research dashboard.

options.label: Role Sleeve
options.thesis: Each role owns a saturated field with a small ranked set of primary tasks.
options.viewport: A full role-color field frames one dominant task and a tidy corner list of secondary work.
options.case: It distinguishes roles well, but cannot carry the platform's dense operational screens alone.
options.risk: The small closed-set composition breaks on large tables and forms.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished learning SaaS shell with conventional cards, a sidebar, dashboards, and role-colored accents.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar sidebar and top bar frame KPI cards, a primary action, and a recent-activity table.
canonCard.risk: Clear and usable, but visually interchangeable with other education dashboards.
